heart.definition: The hollow muscular organ located behind the sternum and between the lungs.

brain.definition: That part of the central nervous system that includes all the higher nervous centers.

lungs.definition: Either of two saclike respiratory organs in the chest of vertebrates.

liver.definition: Large and complicated reddish-brown glandular organ located in the upper right portion of the abdominal cavity.

kidneys.definition: Either of two bean-shaped excretory organs that filter wastes (especially urea) from the blood and excrete them and water in urine.

stomach.definition: An inclination or liking for things involving conflict or difficulty or unpleasantness.

pancreas.definition: A large elongated exocrine gland located behind the stomach.

spleen.definition: A large dark-red oval organ on the left side of the body between the stomach and the diaphragm.

gallbladder.definition: A muscular sac attached to the liver that stores bile (secreted by the liver) until it is needed for digestion.

bladder.definition: A distensible membranous sac (usually containing liquid or gas).

esophagus.definition: The passage between the pharynx and the stomach.

small-intestine.definition: Concerned with the small intestine’s structure, tissue organization, and role in digestion.

large-intestine.definition: Having to do with the colon, the section of the digestive system that forms most of the large intestine.

colon.definition: The part of the large intestine between the cecum and the rectum.

rectum.definition: The terminal section of the alimentary canal.

appendix.definition: A vestigial process that extends from the lower end of the cecum and that resembles a small pouch.

duodenum.definition: The part of the small intestine between the stomach and the jejunum.

jejunum.definition: The part of the small intestine between the duodenum and the ileum.

ileum.definition: The part of the small intestine between the jejunum and the cecum.

trachea.definition: Membranous tube with cartilaginous rings that conveys inhaled air from the larynx to the bronchi.

bronchi.definition: Either of the two main branches of the trachea.

bronchioles.definition: Any of the smallest bronchial ducts.

alveoli.definition: A tiny sac for holding air in the lungs.

diaphragm.definition: A mechanical device in a camera that controls size of aperture of the lens.
diaphragm.exampleUsage: The diaphragm was used during the activity.

larynx.definition: A cartilaginous structure at the top of the trachea.

pharynx.definition: The passage to the stomach and lungs.

nasal-cavity.definition: Either of the two hollow passages inside the nose, located above the mouth and extending back to the throat.

pleura.definition: The thin serous membrane around the lungs and inner walls of the chest.

oxygen.definition: A nonmetallic bivalent element that is normally a colorless odorless tasteless nonflammable diatomic gas.

heart-chamber.definition: One of the four internal spaces of the heart that receive or pump blood.
heart-chamber.exampleUsage: The human heart has four chambers.

aorta.definition: The large trunk artery that carries blood from the left ventricle of the heart to branch arteries.

vein.definition: A blood vessel that carries blood from the capillaries toward the heart.

artery.definition: A blood vessel that carries blood from the heart to the body.

capillary.definition: A tube of small internal diameter.

red-blood-cell.definition: Relating to red blood cells, which carry oxygen from the lungs throughout the body.
red-blood-cell.arabicTranslation: مصطلح طبي أو تشريحي يُسمّى «ريد بلوود كيلل»

white-blood-cell.definition: A blood cell containing a nucleus that mainly protects the body from infection.
white-blood-cell.arabicTranslation: مصطلح طبي أو تشريحي يُسمّى «وهيتي بلوود كيلل»

platelet.definition: Tiny bits of protoplasm found in vertebrate blood.

plasma.definition: The colorless watery fluid of the blood and lymph that contains no cells, but in which the blood cells (erythrocytes, leukocytes, and thrombocytes) are suspended.

pulse.definition: The rhythmic contraction and expansion of the arteries with each beat of the heart.

spinal-cord.definition: Connected with the spine, the column of bones that surrounds and protects the spinal cord.

nerve.definition: Any bundle of nerve fibers running to various organs and tissues of the body.

neuron.definition: A cell that is specialized to conduct nerve impulses.

synapse.definition: The junction between two neurons (axon-to-dendrite) or between a neuron and a muscle.

cerebrum.definition: Anterior portion of the brain consisting of two hemispheres.
cerebrum.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Cerebrum" in an educational description.

cerebellum.definition: A major division of the vertebrate brain.

brain-stem.definition: The lower part of the brain that connects to the spinal cord and helps control vital functions such as breathing and heart rate.
brain-stem.exampleUsage: The brain stem connects the brain with the spinal cord.

signal.definition: An electrical or radio message that carries information.

thyroid.definition: Of or relating to the thyroid gland.

pituitary-gland.definition: A small gland beneath the brain releases hormones that direct growth, metabolism, reproduction, milk production, water balance, and other endocrine glands.
pituitary-gland.arabicTranslation: مصطلح طبي أو تشريحي يُسمّى «بيتويتاري جلاند»

adrenal-gland.definition: Two endocrine glands sit above the kidneys and release hormones that help manage stress, energy use, blood pressure, and the body's salt balance.
adrenal-gland.arabicTranslation: مصطلح طبي أو تشريحي يُسمّى «ادرينال جلاند»

hormone.definition: The secretion of an endocrine gland that is transmitted by the blood to the tissue on which it has a specific effect.

insulin.definition: Hormone secreted by the isles of Langerhans in the pancreas.

testosterone.definition: A potent androgenic hormone produced chiefly by the testes.

estrogen.definition: A general term for female steroid sex hormones that are secreted by the ovary and responsible for typical female sexual characteristics.

metabolism.definition: The organic processes (in a cell or organism) that are necessary for life.

gland.definition: Any of various organs that synthesize substances needed by the body and release it through ducts or directly into the bloodstream.

cortisol.definition: An adrenal-cortex hormone (trade names Hydrocortone or Cortef) that is active in carbohydrate and protein metabolism.
